deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is an administrative note by Gauss: 'Exemplare meiner DEMONSTR. NOV. abgegeben bis zum lezten Nov. 1799 — an … nach …', meaning 'copies of my Demonstratio nova handed out up to the end of November 1799 — to … [sent] to …'.

The work is his Helmstedt doctoral dissertation 'Demonstratio nova theorematis omnes functiones algebraicas rationales integras unius variabilis in factores reales primi vel secundi gradus resolvi posse' (1799). It was his first proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra.

Left column, in alphabetical order, the recipients:
- Academie zu Berlin, Academie zu Petersburg
- Bartels, Butler, Chauvelot, Eschenburg, Euler (presumably J. A. Euler, academy secretary at Petersburg), Facultät zu Helmstedt, Fuß
- Helwig, Herzog (presumably the Duke of Brunswick, his patron), Hindenburg, Kästner, Klügel, Leiste, Mahner(?), Mollweyde, Olbers, Pfaff, Rohde, Schubert, Schul(t)ze
- Societät zu Göttingen, Societät zu London
- v. Stamford, Tamsen(?), v. Tempelhoff, Volkmar, Wood, v. Zach, v. Zimmermann

Names added afterwards in the middle column: Lady Drake, Fischer, LaGrange, Hobert, Ideler, Nationalinstitut (the Paris Institut national), and Seyffer.

Right column, headed 'nach', the destination cities: Berlin, Braunschweig, Bremen, Cambridge, Gotha, Göttingen, Halle, Hamburg, Helmstedt, Leipzig, London, Paris (added), Petersburg, Potsdam, Wolfenbüttel.

Lower right: the names Bartels, Mollweyde, Klügel again, plus pen trials ('S S A'). The page also carries several profile sketches of faces, one carefully shaded.

A faint pencil number at the bottom, transcribed as '36', more likely reads '38'. That would match the count: 31 names in the main column plus 7 interpolated names = 38. My reading; uncertain.

The page documents the circulation of the 1799 dissertation among mathematicians and academies (Lagrange, Kästner, Klügel, Pfaff, Hindenburg, Zach, Olbers, Fuss, Schubert, the Royal Society, the Paris Institut, etc.).

results.what: Distribution list of copies of Gauss's 1799 dissertation (first proof of the fundamental theorem of algebra) to individuals, academies and cities
results.modern_name: Bibliographic/biographical record (reception history of the Demonstratio nova)

deep.surprise_reason: Purely administrative list of dissertation recipients, with doodles. No mathematical content. Of mild biographical interest for the reception of the 1799 dissertation, which is well documented.

checkable.asserts: 31 names in the main alphabetical column plus 7 interpolated recipients (Lady Drake, Fischer, LaGrange, Hobert, Ideler, Nationalinstitut, Seyffer) give 38. This plausibly matches the faint pencil total at the bottom (read here as 38).

transcription_corrections: The faint pencil number after 'v. Zimmermann' more plausibly reads '38' (a tally of recipients) rather than '36'.

Lady Drake, Fischer, LaGrange, Hobert, Ideler, Nationalinstitut and Seyffer are later insertions in a second column, not part of the main alphabetical list. The machine transcription interleaves them.
'Paris' in the right column is an insertion beside London/Petersburg.
The lower-right 'Bartels / Mollweyde / Klügel' is a separate jotting among profile sketches; there are also pen trials ('S S A') not in the transcription.
